adventures.name: Bobcat
adventures.description: The Bobcat Adventure is the first required Adventure on the trail to earn the Tiger badge of rank. Once the Bobcat Adventure is completed, Tigers can start any other of the Adventures in any order.
prerequisites: None — Bobcat is the first required Adventure a new Tiger earns

requirements.text: Get to know the members of your den.

activities.name: A Time to Talk – A Time to Listen
activities.description: The Cub Scout sign is a way to help Cub Scouts learn good manners and communication skills.

activities.name: Den Doodle Tiger
activities.description: The den doodle is a craft project that can be used to track attendance, reward good behavior, and completion of requirements.

activities.name: Den Flag Tiger
activities.description: A den flag is a craft that can bring your den together by getting to know everyone's name and having a symbol that everyone has a part in making.

activities.name: Me Too Name Game
activities.description: Learn how much everyone in the den has in common.

activities.name: Spider Web
activities.description: Members of the den learn about each other as they build a spider web of yarn.

requirements.text: Recite the Scout Oath with your den, including your Tiger adult partner.

activities.name: Cub Scout Land
activities.description: Cub Scouts play Cub Scout Land to learn about each other, the Scout Oath, the Scout Law, and other fundamentals of the Cub Scout program.

activities.name: Tiger Chatterbox
activities.description: Fold a piece of paper into a chatterbox/fortune teller to introduce the Scout Oath to your Cub Scout.

activities.name: Tiger Oath and Law Puzzle
activities.description: Introduce the Scout Oath to Cub Scouts by making a puzzle out of popsicle sticks.

requirements.text: Have your Tiger adult partner or den leader read the Scout Law to you. Demonstrate your understanding of being trustworthy, helpful, or friendly.

activities.name: Don't Wake the Dragon
activities.description: In this game, Cub Scouts have to work together and demonstrate being trustworthy, helpful, and friendly.

activities.name: Tiger Maze
activities.description: Cub Scouts help their adult partner navigate a maze.

activities.name: Tiger Scout Law Bingo
activities.description: Use a bingo card to act out values of the Scout Law.

requirements.text: Demonstrate the Cub Scout sign, Cub Scout salute and Cub Scout handshake. Show how each are used.

activities.name: If You Are Happy Show the Cub Scout Sign
activities.description: Sing the interactive song "If you are happy and you know it" using the Cub Scout sign, handshake, and salute as the actions.

activities.name: Sign, Salute, and Handshake Relay
activities.description: Use a relay race to get Cub Scouts moving and learning the Cub Scout sign, salute, and handshake.

activities.name: Tiger Simon Says
activities.description: Play a game of Simon Says using the actions of the Cub Scout sign, salute, and handshake.

requirements.text: Share with your Tiger adult partner, at a den meeting or at home, a time when you have demonstrated the Cub Scout motto "Do Your Best."

activities.name: Do Your Best Handbook Activity
activities.description: This activity is in the Tiger handbook where Cub Scouts will identify actions that demonstrate the Cub Scout motto "Do Your Best."

activities.name: Do Your Best Handbook Sharing
activities.description: Cub Scouts share with their adult partner a time when they did their best.

requirements.text: At home, with your parent or legal guardian do the activities in the booklet "How to Protect Your Children from Child Abuse: A Parent's Guide."

activities.name: Child Abuse Protection Review Tiger
activities.description: Review the activities in the booklet "How to Protect Your Children from Child Abuse: A Parent's Guide."

adventures.name: Tiger Bites
adventures.description: In this Adventure, Tigers will explore the different food groups, have fun being active, and the importance of rest.

requirements.text: Identify the 5 different food groups.

activities.name: Food Group Tiger Relay
activities.description: Relay race to identify food items and the food group they belong to.

activities.name: My Favorite Foods
activities.description: Cub Scouts draw their favorite food for each of the five good groups.

activities.name: My Favorite Snack
activities.description: Cub Scouts bring and share their favorite food from one of the five food groups.

requirements.text: Practice hand washing. Point out when you should wash your hands.

activities.name: Scout Oath and Law Hand Washing
activities.description: Proper handwashing and learning how long it takes to do a good job.

activities.name: Super Clean Hands! Worksheet
activities.description: Cub Scouts learn about when and how they should wash their hands using a worksheet.

activities.name: When Should I Wash My Hands Game
activities.description: Cub Scouts learn about when they should wash their hands in this active game.

requirements.text: Be active for 30 minutes.

activities.name: Tiger Obstacle Course
activities.description: Obstacle Course.

activities.name: Tiger Red Light Green Light
activities.description: Play Red Light / Green Light.

activities.name: Tiger Soccer
activities.description: Play Soccer with the Den.

requirements.text: Practice methods that help you sleep.

activities.name: Sleep Like a Star! Worksheet
activities.description: Cub Scouts learn about how to get the best rest using a worksheet.

activities.name: Tiger Get Ready for Bed
activities.description: Make a bedtime routine to help get enough sleep using the activity in the Tiger handbook.

activities.name: Tiger Time to Sleep
activities.description: Cub Scouts with their parent or legal guardian establish a good bedtime.

adventures.name: Tiger's Roar
adventures.description: In partnership with the Barbara Sinatra Children's Center Foundation, Tigers will learn about the "Protect Yourself Rules" and other skills needed to stay safe.

requirements.text: With permission from your parent or legal guardian watch the Protect Yourself Rules video for the Tiger rank.

activities.name: Protect Yourself Rules Video Tiger
activities.description: Watch the Protect Yourself Rules video with your parent or legal guardian.

requirements.text: With your Tiger adult partner, demonstrate Shout, Run, Tell as explained in the Protect Yourself Rules video.

activities.name: Police Officer Visit
activities.description: Cub Scouts learn about personal safety from a police officer.

activities.name: Shout Run and Tell Worksheet
activities.description: Tigers will complete a shout Run Tell worksheet.

activities.name: Shout, Run, Tell Relay
activities.description: A relay race where Cub Scouts will demonstrate Shout, Run, Tell.

requirements.text: With your Tiger adult partner, demonstrate how to access emergency services.

activities.name: Emergency Services 911 Relay Race
activities.description: Emergency Services 911 Safety Relay.

activities.name: Smart Phone Emergency Services
activities.description: Teach Cub Scouts how to use a smart phone to reach emergency services (911).

activities.name: Voice Activated Devices Emergency Services
activities.description: Teach your Cub Scout how to use your home voice-activated devices to contact emergency services.

requirements.text: With your Tiger adult partner, demonstrate that you know what to do if you get lost or separated.

activities.name: Emergency Whistle Testing
activities.description: Cub Scouts will blow whistles and demonstrate how to use the whistle if they get lost.

activities.name: Hide and Seek
activities.description: A twist on hide and seek where after 5 minutes Cub Scouts use methods learned to be found.

activities.name: Pinewood Derby® Driver's License
activities.description: Cub Scouts create a Pinewood Derby® driver's license that doubles as an ID card.

adventures.name: Tiger Circles
adventures.description: In this Adventure, the Tigers learn about their family by exploring the faith traditions and celebrations that make being part of their family special. Tigers may earn this Adventure by completing the requirements OR by earning the religious emblem of their choosing.

requirements.text: With your parent or legal guardian talk about your family's faith traditions. Identify three holidays or celebrations that are part of your family's faith traditions. Draw a picture of your favorite family's faith tradition holiday or celebration.

activities.name: My Family Celebrations
activities.description: Cub Scouts will identify three celebrations that match their family creating a My Family Celebrations sheet.

activities.name: My Family Traditions Worksheet
activities.description: Students will learn about their family's faith traditions by identifying three celebrations and illustrating their favorite.

activities.name: Tiger Circles Passport
activities.description: Complete the Family and Reverence activities at home with your family.

activities.name: Tiger Holiday Drawing
activities.description: Draw and color a favorite faith tradition holiday or celebration.

activities.name: Tree of Reverence – Tiger
activities.description: This activity will set a calm and reflective tone as Cub Scouts and their families arrive for the Reverence Adventure. It encourages participants to think about and express what reverence means to them in a creative way.

requirements.text: With your family, attend a religious service OR other gathering that shows how your family expresses Family & Reverence.

activities.name: Tiger Circles Passport
activities.description: Complete the Family and Reverence activities at home with your family.

activities.name: Tiger Religious Celebration
activities.description: Cub Scouts attend a religious celebration with their family.

activities.name: Tiger Religious Service
activities.description: Attend a religious service with your family.

activities.name: Tiger Veterans Day
activities.description: Attend a Veterans Day event with your den.

requirements.text: Carry out an act of kindness.

activities.name: Tiger A Note of Kindness
activities.description: Make a card of kindness to give to someone special.

activities.name: Tiger Be Kind at Home
activities.description: Cub Scouts perform an act of kindness at home.

activities.name: Tiger Be Kind at School
activities.description: Cub Scouts show kindness at school by inviting someone who is alone to join them.

activities.name: Tiger Circles Passport
activities.description: Complete the Family and Reverence activities at home with your family.

adventures.name: Team Tiger
adventures.description: Citizenship is one of the four aims of the Scouting America program. For Tigers citizenship begins at home and their den. They will explore how they can contribute to their home and community.

requirements.text: Play a game with your den, or family members, that has a set of rules. Discuss why rules are important to the game you are playing.

activities.name: Card Game – Go Fish
activities.description: Play a game of Go Fish!

activities.name: Tigers Play Cornhole
activities.description: Play a game of cornhole.

activities.name: Tigers Play Kickball
activities.description: Play a game of kickball.

requirements.text: With your Tiger Adult Partner, choose a job that will help your team. Follow through by doing that job at least once.

activities.name: Tiger Flag Ceremony
activities.description: Participate in a flag-raising ceremony for your school.

activities.name: Tiger Greeter
activities.description: Tiger den serve as greeters for the pack meeting.

activities.name: Tigers Help Clean Up
activities.description: Help set up and clean up for a pack meeting.

requirements.text: Play a game that requires at least 2 teams with your den, or two other family members. Afterwards discuss what it means to be part of a team and what makes a good team member.

activities.name: Tiger Charades
activities.description: Play a game of charades with your den.

activities.name: Tiger Volleyball
activities.description: Play a game of Tiger Volleyball.

activities.name: Tiger Wiffle Ball
activities.description: Play a game of wiffle ball with the den.

requirements.text: Participate in a service project.

activities.name: 10,000 for the Troops – Tiger
activities.description: Cub Scouts participate in a special nation-wide project to create holiday cards for military personnel.

activities.name: Board Game Collection
activities.description: Collect game boards for a community center.

activities.name: Sock Drive
activities.description: Sock drive service project.

activities.name: Tiger Scouting for Food
activities.description: Participate in your Council-sponsored Scouting for Food event.

adventures.name: Tigers in the Wild
adventures.description: Tigers and adult partners will take a walk to explore the outdoors. Along the way, they can learn about domesticated and wild animals.

requirements.text: Identify the Cub Scout Six Essentials. Show what you do with each item.

activities.name: Grab the Six Essentials
activities.description: Relay race for Cub Scouts to identify the Cub Scout Six Essentials.

activities.name: Is It a Cub Scout Essential?
activities.description: Cub Scouts pick out the Cub Scout six essentials from mix of outdoor equipment.

activities.name: Outdoor Code in a Flash
activities.description: Flash card activity to introduce Cub Scouts to the Outdoor Code.

requirements.text: With your den leader or Tiger adult partner, learn about the Outdoor Code.

activities.name: Outdoor Code Puzzle
activities.description: Cub Scouts use their Tiger handbook to create an Outdoor Code puzzle.

activities.name: Sing the Outdoor Code
activities.description: Cub Scouts will learn about the Outdoor Code by singing the Outdoor Code Song.

activities.name: The Four C's of the Outdoor Code
activities.description: The four C's is a method of introducing the Outdoor Code.

requirements.text: With your den, pack, or family, take a walk outside spending for at least 20 minutes exploring the outdoors with your Cub Scout Six Essentials. While outside, identify things that you see with your Tiger adult partner that are natural and things that are manmade.

activities.name: 5 Step Seek
activities.description: Adult partners give a clue to something they see outside as Cub Scouts guess what it is and if it is natural or manmade.

activities.name: I Spy Natural or Manmade
activities.description: A game of I Spy that includes objects that are natural or manmade.

activities.name: Natural or Manmade by the Numbers
activities.description: Cub Scouts and adult partners work together to identify as many things they can that are natural and manmade.

requirements.text: Identify common animals that are found where you live. Learn which of those animals is domesticated and which animal is wild. Draw a picture of your favorite animal.

activities.name: Animals I know
activities.description: Cub Scouts identify animals they have seen and identify if they are wild or domestic.

activities.name: My Favorite Animals
activities.description: Cub Scouts draw their favorite domesticated and wild animal.

activities.name: Stuffed Animal Relay Race
activities.description: Using stuffed animals Cub Scouts identify if the animal is wild or domesticated.

activities.name: Wild or Domestic Sorting Game
activities.description: Cub Scouts will sort animal cards into a Venn diagram, distinguishing between wild, domestic, or both. Then, they will draw their favorite animal.

requirements.text: Look for a tree where you live. Describe how this tree is helpful.

activities.name: Leaf and Bark Rubbing
activities.description: Make a leaf and bark rubbing of a tree.

activities.name: Pinecone Bird Feeder
activities.description: Make a pinecone bird feeder and place it in a tree.

activities.name: Tiger Tree Planting
activities.description: Plant a tree.

adventures.name: Champions for Nature
adventures.description: As part of the World Organization of the Scouting Movement, this program is part of a global effort to teach youth about the conservation of natural resources. This includes participating in a service project.

requirements.text: Discover the difference between renewable natural resources and non-renewable natural resources.

activities.name: Identify Renewable and Non-renewable
activities.description: Identify pictures of items that are renewable resources and non-renewable resources.

activities.name: Renewable Resource Walk
activities.description: Walk outside and point out items that are made from or use renewable resources and things that are made from or use non-renewable resources.

activities.name: Renewable Show and Tell
activities.description: Cub Scouts bring everyday items from home and the den will sort them as made from renewable or non-renewable resources.

requirements.text: Learn about the 3 R's: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle.

activities.name: Reduce, Reuse, or Recycle?
activities.description: Play a guessing game of items that can be recycled, reused, or reduced.

activities.name: Solar Powered S'more Oven
activities.description: Reduce the use of electricity by making a solar powered oven.

activities.name: The 3 R's of Our Den Meeting Space
activities.description: Take a walk around your den meeting location and point out what items can be recycled, reused, and/or reduced.

requirements.text: Discover what happens to the garbage in your community.

activities.name: Den Outing to Waste Management
activities.description: Den outing to a waste management facility.

activities.name: The Journey of a Piece of Garbage
activities.description: Cub Scouts will learn about the journey a piece of garbage takes and then act it out in a skit.

requirements.text: Participate in a conservation project.

activities.name: Clean Waterways
activities.description: A nationwide initiative aimed at addressing the critical issue of waterway and marine debris, offering Scouts the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on the health of our waterways and ecosystems.

activities.name: Clothing Drive – Reuse
activities.description: Conduct a clothing drive for a local charity.

activities.name: Plant It and the Butterflies will Come
activities.description: Plant a butterfly garden.

activities.name: Plastic Bottle Planter – Reuse
activities.description: Turn a plastic bottle into an indoor planter.

adventures.name: Curiosity, Intrigue, and Magical Mysteries
adventures.description: A fun Adventure where Tigers learn how to perform a magic trick and create a secret code.

requirements.text: Learn a magic trick. Practice the trick. Share the trick with you den or family members.

activities.name: Coin Through a Neckerchief
activities.description: Pass a coin magically though your Tiger neckerchief.

activities.name: Cub Scout Magic Book
activities.description: Use the Cub Scout Magic book to identify a trick for Cub Scouts to learn and perform.

activities.name: The Disappearing Knot
activities.description: Tie a knot that disappears.

requirements.text: Demonstrate how a magic trick works to your den, family or Tiger adult partner.

activities.name: Magic Show
activities.description: Using the magic trick learned in requirement 1, conduct a magic show.

requirements.text: Write your name in secret code.

activities.name: Computer Name
activities.description: Use binary to spell your name.

activities.name: My Secret Code Part 1
activities.description: Cub Scouts will create their own unique secret code.

activities.name: Pig Pen Code
activities.description: Using the Pig Pen Code write your name.

requirements.text: Write a message with the code. Challenge your den, family or Tiger adult partner to read your coded message.

activities.name: My Secret Code Part 2
activities.description: Using the secret code created in the activity My Secret Code Part 1 write a message and have Tiger adult partners decode the message.

adventures.name: Designed by Tiger
adventures.description: Tigers will discover the fundamentals of the engineering process of designing, building, and improving.

requirements.text: Think about something that you would like to build. Draw a picture of what the final project should look like.

activities.name: My Project Plan Drawing
activities.description: Draw something that you are going to build before you build it.

requirements.text: Using your drawing as a guide, build the project.

activities.name: Crossing the River
activities.description: Cub Scouts build a model of something that will help the den cross a river.

activities.name: Cub Scout Land
activities.description: Make a model of an amusement park ride.

requirements.text: When completed, discuss with your Tiger adult partner what could be done to improve your project.

activities.name: Room For Improvement
activities.description: Identify ways that your project could be improved.

requirements.text: Make the improvement to your project.

activities.name: Making it Better
activities.description: Make improvement on the model made in requirement 2 based on feedback from the den.

requirements.text: Make a drawing of your final project.

activities.name: Comparing Start to Finish
activities.description: Compare the original drawing to the final project model.

adventures.name: Fish On
adventures.description: With their family or den and adult partner, Tigers will learn the basics of fishing and go on a fishing adventure.

requirements.text: With your den or Tiger adult partner, identify the body of water where you will go fishing.

activities.name: Department of Natural Resources Visit
activities.description: Cub Scouts will meet with a representative from the local Department of Natural Resources.

activities.name: Flashy Fish Homes
activities.description: Use flashcards to identify local fish.

activities.name: Our Fishing Spot
activities.description: Using a local map identify the spot where you will go fishing and the fish that live in that body of water.

requirements.text: With your Tiger adult partner, learn the rules of fishing safely.

activities.name: Dry Run Fishing
activities.description: Using fishing poles, practice the fishing rules before going on the fishing adventure.

activities.name: Fishing Safety Match
activities.description: Learn the fishing safety rules by completing the activity in the Tiger handbook.

requirements.text: Draw a picture of the type of fish you think lives in the water where you are going fishing.

activities.name: Color a Fish
activities.description: Cub Scouts will learn about local fish species as they color.

activities.name: Craft a Fish
activities.description: Cub Scouts will craft a realistic fish out of recyclable materials.

activities.name: Scales and Sketches
activities.description: Using the Tiger handbook draw two fish that live in the water you are going fishing.

requirements.text: Go fishing with your Tiger adult partner.

activities.name: Fish On!
activities.description: Go fishing with your den.

adventures.name: Floats and Boats
adventures.description: Discovering what floats and how to make a model boat are the key activities in this Adventure.

requirements.text: Identify five different types of boats.

activities.name: Color the Boats
activities.description: Color the boats in the Tiger handbook.

activities.name: Model Boats
activities.description: Identify different types of boats using models.

activities.name: Visit a Marina
activities.description: See real boats by visiting a marina.

requirements.text: Identify five things that float and five things that do not float.

activities.name: Floating or Sinking?
activities.description: In a tub discover things that float and things that do not.

requirements.text: Build or create a model boat and float it on the water. This can be made from recycled materials or other items.

activities.name: Crafty Boat
activities.description: Make a model boat from recycled and craft supplies.

activities.name: Paper Boat
activities.description: Fold paper to make a boat using the Tiger handbook.

activities.name: Raingutter Regatta™ Floating Boat
activities.description: Make a Raingutter Regatta™ boat.

requirements.text: Show that you can put on and fasten a life jacket correctly and learn when it is safe to enter a boat.

activities.name: Captain Says
activities.description: Cub Scouts play a game to learn about wearing a life jacket and boating safety.

activities.name: Life Jacket Relay
activities.description: Once Cub Scouts learn how to proper fit a life jacket conduct a relay race.

activities.name: Proper Fit – Proper Safety
activities.description: Cub Scouts try on a properly fitted life jacket.

adventures.name: Good Knights
adventures.description: Tigers will have fun making their own shield or coat of arms and even a castle.

requirements.text: Discuss with your den or Tiger adult partner what it means to have courteous behavior, how a knight behaves. Tell another Tiger which points of the Scout Law help you to have the same Knightly behavior.

activities.name: A Knight Says
activities.description: Cub Scouts will practice being courteous and kind—like knights—by listening for "please" during a fun variation of the game of Simon Says.

activities.name: Courteous Knights
activities.description: Cub Scouts will act out acts of being courteous and other points of the Scout Law.

activities.name: Modern Knights
activities.description: Have a guest speaker from one of the armed services come to speak about the values and creed of their branch.

requirements.text: Create a shield that can be for your den or a personal shield.

activities.name: Den Shield
activities.description: Working together as a den make a den shield.

activities.name: Personal Little Shield
activities.description: Make a personal little shield out of plywood and decorate it with paint.

activities.name: Personal Shield
activities.description: Cub Scouts make a personal shield from project board.

requirements.text: Using recycled and other materials, design and build a small castle in your den or at home.

activities.name: Building Sandcastles
activities.description: Use a sandbox for the den to create a den sandcastle.

activities.name: Castle Made of Building Blocks
activities.description: Make a castle using modular building blocks such as Legos.

activities.name: Yesterdays Trash is Todays Castle
activities.description: Using recycled or reused materials, build a model castle.

requirements.text: Do a Good Turn.

activities.name: Knights Do a Good Turn Like Scouts Do
activities.description: This is not a service project it is simply a good turn, a good deed for someone else.

adventures.name: Let's Camp
adventures.description: Here is the opportunity for Tigers and their adult partners to go on an overnight campout.

requirements.text: Learn about the buddy system and how it works in the outdoors.

activities.name: Back to Back Buddies
activities.description: Cub Scout buddies work together to stand up while sitting on the floor back-to-back.

activities.name: Stay with Your Buddy Challenge
activities.description: Cub Scouts will understand and practice the buddy system by staying with a partner during a movement-based activity.

activities.name: Who is Being A Buddy?
activities.description: Using an activity sheet identify who is using the buddy system.

requirements.text: Before going on the overnight campout, discuss what type of weather is expected and what type of clothes you should wear.

activities.name: Dress the Paper Cub Scout
activities.description: Cub Scouts will pick the correct outfit for their paper Cub Scout based on the weather.

activities.name: What is the Weather Like There?
activities.description: Cub Scouts look at a weather report for the campout.

activities.name: What to Wear? What to Wear? When Camping
activities.description: Cub Scouts pick out clothes that are appropriate for different types of weather.

requirements.text: Pack up your Cub Scout Six Essentials for the campout.

activities.name: Six Essentials Scavenger Hunt
activities.description: Cub Scouts go on a scavenger hunt to collect Cub Scout Six Essentials.

activities.name: Six Essentials Shopping Spree
activities.description: Provide Cub Scouts their own Cub Scout Six Essentials.

requirements.text: Learn a camping skill.

activities.name: Flashlight Tiger Hunt
activities.description: Learn about the different flashlight and flashlight etiquette.

activities.name: My First Knot
activities.description: Cub Scouts will learn about the square knot and attempt to tie it.

activities.name: Tent Time!
activities.description: Cub Scout and adult partners will practice setting up a tent.

requirements.text: Attend a council or district Cub Scout overnight camp or attend a campout with your pack.

activities.name: Council Camping Tiger
activities.description: Go camping at your local council camp.

activities.name: Pack Camping Tiger
activities.description: Go camping with your pack.

adventures.name: Race Time
adventures.description: The most popular events in Cub Scouting are found in this Adventure, the Pinewood Derby® and the Raingutter Regatta™. Tigers and adult partners work together to build and race either a car or boat.

requirements.text: With your Tiger adult partner, assemble and decorate either a Pinewood Derby® car or a Raingutter Regatta™ boat.

activities.name: Pinewood Derby® Car Build Day Tiger
activities.description: Den or pack provides a build day for Cub Scouts.

activities.name: Raingutter Regatta™ Boat Build Day Tiger
activities.description: Den or pack provides a build day for Cub Scouts.

requirements.text: Learn the rules of the race for the vehicle chosen in requirement 1.

activities.name: Race Memory Tiger
activities.description: Memory Game using Pinewood Derby® or Raingutter Regatta™ Rules.

activities.name: Race Ready Or Not Sorting Game
activities.description: Cub Scouts will recognize behaviors that follow race rules by completing a sorting activity.

activities.name: Rule or Not a Rule
activities.description: Cub Scouts determine if statements are rules or not rules.

requirements.text: Before the race, discuss with your Tiger adult partner how you will demonstrate good sportsmanship during the race.

activities.name: Act Like a Good Sport Tiger
activities.description: Cub Scouts will act out through role playing how to be a good sport during the race.

activities.name: My Race Day Promise
activities.description: Cub Scouts will plan what they will say to situations on race day.

activities.name: Race Pledge
activities.description: Cub Scouts will commit to demonstrating sportsmanship.

requirements.text: With your Tiger adult partner, participate in a Pinewood Derby® or a Raingutter Regatta™.

activities.name: Pinewood Derby® Race Tiger
activities.description: Conduct a Pinewood Derby® car race.

activities.name: Raingutter Regatta™ Tiger
activities.description: Conduct a Raingutter Regatta™.

adventures.name: Rolling Tigers
adventures.description: With their family or den, Tigers learn bike safety and go on a bike ride. Bikes, training wheels, tricycles, and adaptive bikes are welcome.

requirements.text: Learn the ABC's of bike gear (air, brakes, chain.)

activities.name: Talk With A Pro
activities.description: A guest speaker who is an expert in cycling demonstrates the ABC's of bike gear.

activities.name: The ABC's of Bike Gear
activities.description: Cub Scouts and adult partners will learn about the ABC's of bike gear using an example bike.

activities.name: The ABC's of My Bike
activities.description: Using their own bike or one borrowed, Cub Scout and adult partners learn the ABC's of bike gear.

requirements.text: With your den or Tiger adult partner, learn about the safety gear you should use while riding a bicycle.

activities.name: Ask the Pro
activities.description: A guest speaker who is an expert in cycling demonstrates the ABC's of bike safety gear.

activities.name: Check My Bike Gear
activities.description: Cub Scouts check their own safety gear.

activities.name: Safe Rider Gear Checklist
activities.description: Cub Scouts will create a "Safe Rider" by choosing the correct safety gear.

requirements.text: With your den or Tiger adult partner, learn the safety rules to follow when riding a bicycle.

activities.name: Chalk It Up Bike Rodeo
activities.description: Create a bike safety course using chalk patterns on the ground.

activities.name: Learn from the Pro
activities.description: A guest speaker who is an expert in cycling discusses the safety rules to follow when riding a bike.

activities.name: When to Walk and When to Ride
activities.description: Review safety rules for bike riding.

requirements.text: With your den or Tiger adult partner, demonstrate proper hand signals.

activities.name: Signals with the Pro
activities.description: A guest speaker who is an expert in cycling demonstrates the hand signals to use while riding a bike.

activities.name: Simon Says – Turn Left, Turn Right
activities.description: Play Simon Says using the bike hand signals for turning left and turning right.

activities.name: Traffic Light Freeze
activities.description: Play a game to practice the hand signals to use while riding a bike.

requirements.text: With your Tiger adult partner or family, ride a bike or begin learning how to ride a bike.

activities.name: I Want To Ride My Bicycle!
activities.description: Take a bike ride with your den.

adventures.name: Safe and Smart
adventures.description: Tigers will learn about fire safety and other ways to prepare and respond to emergencies.

requirements.text: Memorize your address. Recite it to your Tiger adult partner or den leader.

activities.name: BINGO! That is Where I Live
activities.description: Cub Scouts learn their address by putting it to the tune of BINGO.

activities.name: In Case of an Emergency
activities.description: Tigers will complete an activity with their, name, address, emergency contact number, and 911 to post in their home.

activities.name: Send Me a Letter
activities.description: Cub Scouts learn their address so they can mail themselves a letter.

requirements.text: Memorize an emergency contact's phone number. Recite it to your Tiger adult partner or den leader.

activities.name: Cheerio My Number
activities.description: Using Cheerios, Cub Scouts learn their emergency contact number.

activities.name: Match my Number
activities.description: Cub Scouts unscramble numbers written on index cards to make their phone number.

activities.name: Sing a Phone Song
activities.description: Cub Scouts learn to memorize their phone number through a song.

requirements.text: Show you can Stop, Drop and Roll.

activities.name: Fire Tag
activities.description: Cub Scouts practice "Stop, Drop, and Roll" while playing a game of tag.

activities.name: Stop Drop and Roll Crown
activities.description: Cub Scouts will practice Stop, Drop, and Roll and then color a crown to wear.

activities.name: Stop Drop and Roll Relay
activities.description: Cub Scouts learn how to Stop Drop and Roll by playing a relay race.

requirements.text: With your Tiger adult partner or den leader, create a fire escape plan for your home or den meeting place. Include your outside meet-up spot. Practice the escape route you would take.

activities.name: Den Meeting Exit Plan
activities.description: The den will work to develop an evacuation plan for their meeting location and identify a meet-up spot.

activities.name: It's Time to Get Out!
activities.description: Create an escape route.

activities.name: Stuffed Animal Fire Escape Practice
activities.description: Cub Scouts with their adult partners will teach stuffed animals how to escape from a dangerous place in the event of a fire.

requirements.text: With your Tiger adult partner, find the location of the smoke detectors in your home or den meeting place. Confirm they are working properly.

activities.name: Where There Is Smoke
activities.description: Locate smoke detectors in your home.

requirements.text: With your Tiger adult partner or den leader, learn why matches and lighters are only for adults.

activities.name: Spread Like Wildfire
activities.description: The den will learn how fast fire can spread and why starting fires can cause harm.

activities.name: Stop, Don't Touch, Tell an Adult
activities.description: Cub Scouts will play a game where they stop, don't touch, and tell an adult if they see matches or a lighter.

activities.name: Visit a Fire Station
activities.description: Cub Scouts visit a fire station to learn about why matches and lighters should be used only by responsible adults.

requirements.text: Visit an emergency responder station or have an emergency responder visit your den.

activities.name: Meet Emergency Responders
activities.description: Plan a visit to a fire station or other emergency response station.

adventures.name: Sky is the Limit
adventures.description: Astronomy is the focus of this Adventure as Tigers explore the night sky and discover constellations.

requirements.text: Observe the night sky with your den or Tiger adult partner. Talk about the items you see or might see there.

activities.name: My Night Sky Adventure
activities.description: Cub Scouts will observe the night sky and record their observations.

activities.name: Night Sky Scavenger Hunt
activities.description: Conduct a scavenger hunt of what is in the night sky.

activities.name: Visit a Planetarium
activities.description: Cub Scouts visit a planetarium to observe the night sky.

requirements.text: Look at distant objects through a telescope, binoculars, or camera. Show how to focus the device you choose.

activities.name: I Can See the Stars
activities.description: The basics of how to use a telescope.

requirements.text: Observe in the sky or select from a book, chart, computer, or electronic device two constellations that are easy to see in the night sky. With your den or Tiger adult partner, find out the constellation name and how to identify them. Create a picture of one of the constellations.

activities.name: Pictures in the Sky
activities.description: Identify and observe two constellations in the night sky.

activities.name: Sticker Constellations
activities.description: Cub Scouts will look at constellation flashcards and pick their favorite to recreate in sticker art.

requirements.text: Create a homemade model of a constellation.

activities.name: Can-stellation
activities.description: Make a model constellation out of a tin can.

activities.name: Edible Constellation
activities.description: Make an edible model of a constellation.

activities.name: Glowing Constellation
activities.description: Glow in the dark painting of constellations.

adventures.name: Stories in Shapes
adventures.description: Tigers will explore math through the discovery of art and how shapes and symbols can tell a story.

requirements.text: Explore art in your community.

activities.name: Art on Display
activities.description: Visit an art museum.

activities.name: Art Trail
activities.description: Take a walk in a neighborhood with public art such as outdoor murals, statues, and sculptures.

activities.name: Virtual Tour of Art
activities.description: Coordinate a virtual tour of the Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

requirements.text: Look closely at art or a picture of art with your den or Tiger adult partner. Decide what you like about the art, and share your ideas with your den, family or Tiger adult partner.

activities.name: Art on Display part 2
activities.description: This activity is designed to be done in combination with requirement 1 and the Art on Display activity at an art museum.

activities.name: Art Trail part 2
activities.description: This activity is designed to be done in combination with requirement 1 and the Art Trail activity.

activities.name: Virtual Tour of Art 2
activities.description: This activity is designed to be done in combination with requirement 1 and the Virtual Tour of Art activity.

requirements.text: Create a piece of art using shapes.

activities.name: Folding Art
activities.description: Make an origami cat.

activities.name: My Art From Shapes
activities.description: Using the shapes in the Tiger Handbook (page 55) make a piece of art.

activities.name: Spiral Art
activities.description: Make a drawing using a spiral stencil set.

activities.name: Tangram Animals
activities.description: Using tangrams make animal shapes.

requirements.text: Learn how to spell your name in Braille and sign language.

activities.name: Get To Know Me and Sign Language
activities.description: Invite someone who is deaf or an interpreter for the deaf to visit the den.

activities.name: Reading with Your Hands
activities.description: Using puffy round stickers spell your name in braille.

activities.name: The Art of Sign Language
activities.description: Cub Scouts will learn about American Sign Language and how to sign their name.

adventures.name: Summertime Fun
adventures.description: Stay active in the summertime by attending den or pack events, Cub Scout Day Camp, or Resident Camp.

requirements.text: Anytime during May through August participate in a total of three Cub Scout activities.

activities.name: Council activity Tiger
activities.description: Participate in an activity with your council.

activities.name: Den activity Tiger
activities.description: Participate in an activity with your den.

activities.name: Pack activity Tiger
activities.description: Participate in an activity with your pack.

adventures.name: Tech All Around
adventures.description: Tigers will identify technology that is common in most homes and discover how technology has improved along with safety rules around technology they come in contact with.

requirements.text: Discover technology around your home, meeting place, or neighborhood.

activities.name: Detective Walk
activities.description: Cub Scouts will identify technology in their everyday lives.

activities.name: Technology at Home
activities.description: Discover technology at home.

activities.name: Tigers Hunt for Technology
activities.description: Scavenger hunt for technology.

requirements.text: Discover ways that digital technology can make life easier.

activities.name: Low Tech vs. High Tech
activities.description: Cub Scouts complete activities without using technology and with the help of technology.

activities.name: Technology Charades
activities.description: A game of charades that identifies how technology has made life easier.

activities.name: The Way It Was
activities.description: Tiger adult partners share what life was like before modern technology.

requirements.text: Identify an item of digital technology you use at home. Demonstrate to your adult partner how you use it safely.

activities.name: Be Safe with Technology Tiger
activities.description: Discuss digital technology that the Cub Scout has access to and proper use.

requirements.text: With your parent or legal guardian, set up a policy for digital devices.

activities.name: Smart and Safe with Technology
activities.description: Cub Scouts create rules for the use of digital devices.

adventures.name: Tiger Tag
adventures.description: Learning teamwork, good sportsmanship, and having fun with their family or den by playing outdoor games or sports is packed into this Adventure, including attending a sporting event together.

requirements.text: Play an active game with your den. Share with your Tiger adult partner or your den why you like this game.

activities.name: Tiger Blob Tag
activities.description: Play Blob Tag.

activities.name: Tiger Duck Duck Goose
activities.description: Play a game of duck, duck, goose.

activities.name: Tiger Hide and Seek
activities.description: Play a game of hide and seek.

requirements.text: Play a relay game with your den. Share with your Tiger adult partner or your den why you like this game.

activities.name: Tiger Dress Up Relay
activities.description: Play Tiger Dress-Up relay.

activities.name: Tiger Passing the Ball Relay
activities.description: Play Passing the Ball Relay race.

activities.name: Tiger Ping-pong Relay
activities.description: Play Ping-pong ball relay.

requirements.text: Discuss what it means to be a good sport in a game with your Tiger adult partner or other Tigers.

activities.name: Referee Visit
activities.description: Invite someone who is a referee (volunteer or professional) to discuss sportsmanship with the den.

activities.name: Sportsmanship Practice
activities.description: Cub Scouts will learn about and practice good sportsmanship.

activities.name: Who is Being a Good Sport
activities.description: Cub Scouts complete activity in the Tiger handbook to identify good sportsmanship.

requirements.text: Attend a sporting event.

activities.name: Tiger Catch the Game On TV
activities.description: Watch a sporting event on television.

activities.name: Tiger Friday Night Lights
activities.description: Attend a high school football game.

activities.name: Tiger Let's Play Ball
activities.description: Attend a professional baseball game.

activities.name: Tiger Youth Sporting Event
activities.description: Attend a youth sporting event.

adventures.name: Tiger-iffic!
adventures.description: Taking turns and following the rules of the game is the lesson behind this fun Adventure as Tigers play by the rules.

requirements.text: Play at least two different games by yourself; one may be a video game.

activities.name: Disc Golf and Soccer Golf
activities.description: Set up a golf course to play disc and soccer golf.

activities.name: Scout Life Games and Puzzles
activities.description: Cub Scouts play a video game on the Scout Life Magazine website and complete a crossword puzzle.

activities.name: Seven Up and Indoor Bowling
activities.description: Two fun games that only take one player, indoor bowling and seven up.

requirements.text: Play a board game or another inside game with one or more members of your den or family.

activities.name: Catch Them All!
activities.description: Conduct a Pokémon tournament.

activities.name: Checkers Tournament
activities.description: Conduct a Checkers tournament.

activities.name: Den Game Time
activities.description: Members of the den bring their favorite board or card game to play.

requirements.text: With other members of your den or family, invent a game, or change the rules of a game you know, and play the game.

activities.name: Checkers with a Twist
activities.description: Change the rules to checkers by allowing another turn if you take another players checker.

activities.name: Game Remix
activities.description: Cub Scouts and their adult partners will work together in small groups to remix the rules of a familiar game. Then, they will play their remixed games with the rest of the den.

activities.name: My Cub Scout Game
activities.description: Make a board game based on Cub Scouting.

requirements.text: Play a team game with your den or family.

activities.name: Let's Bowl!
activities.description: Take the den bowling.

activities.name: Tiger Balloon Volleyball
activities.description: Play a game of balloon volleyball.

activities.name: Tiger Den Kickball
activities.description: Play a game of kickball.

adventures.name: Tigers in the Water
adventures.description: Tigers will learn how to stay safe in the water and get comfortable with being in the water. Tigers can earn this Adventure by completing the requirements OR by taking swim lessons.

requirements.text: Learn about the swimming safety rules that you need to follow.

activities.name: Tiger Safe Swim Defense
activities.description: Cub Scouts will identify the Safe Swim Defense.

requirements.text: Demonstrate how to enter the swimming area properly.

activities.name: Swim Area Safety
activities.description: Before going swimming Cub Scouts learn how to properly enter the swimming area.

requirements.text: With your Tiger adult partner as your buddy, be active in water depths matching your ability for 20 minutes.

activities.name: Go Swimming
activities.description: Take your den and go swimming.

requirements.text: Place your face in the water and blow bubbles.

activities.name: Bubbles in the Water
activities.description: While in the pool Cub Scouts will blow bubbles in the water.

requirements.text: Demonstrate a flutter kick.

activities.name: Flutter Kicking
activities.description: Demonstrate the flutter kick using the side of the pool for assistance.

requirements.text: Demonstrate how to exit the swimming area properly.

activities.name: Swim Time Is Over
activities.description: Demonstrate the importance of exiting the pool safely and removing buddy tag from the buddy board.
